newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-TYSON SUSPENDED BY NEVADA ATHLETIC COMMISSION.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-TYSON SUSPENDED BY NEVADA ATHLETIC COMMISSION.

text.p: The Nevada State Athletic Commission Tuesday kept Mike Tyson suspended and his $30 million fight purse withheld, pending a disciplinary hearing next week over his biting of Evander Holyfield in Saturday's world heavyweight championship bout.
The commission ordered Don King Productions to provide a check for $29,824,600, representing Tyson's purse, to be deposited in an interest-bearing account pending the outcome of the hearing.
The Nevada attorney general's office has yet to draw up a formal complaint over the incident on behalf of the commission, and a period of three working days must pass before the hearing may be held.
That would set the hearing for next Tuesday or Wednesday at the earliest, since the July 4 Independence Day holiday is observed on Friday.
Tyson has waived the 30-day period he is allowed under the regulations to address a complaint so that the issue can be settled as quickly as possible.

Deputy District attorney Joe Rolston told reporters that two code violations would be involved in the complaint, one alleging that Tyson is "guilty of a foul or unsportsmanlike conduct," and the other alleging that the fighter is "guilty of conduct which discredits boxing."
Tyson did not attend the emergency hearing held at the Las Vegas Council Chambers at City Hall.
Tyson's attorney, Eckley Keach, referred to the boxer's public apology on Monday and said: "He will place his fate in their hands.
"There is no way we are going to argue that he shouldn't be fined or suspended."

Rolston said Tyson could be fined a maximum of $250,000, or be both fined and suspended by the commission. If Tyson's license is revoked over the incident, Tyson could be fined up to 10 percent of his purse, or nearly $3 million.

Tyson pleaded for his professional future on Monday when he apologised for "snapping" in the ring and begged forgiveness following his disqualification for twice biting Holyfield's ears and taking a chunk out of his right one.
He said he would accept the punishment to be handed down, asking only that it not be a lifetime ban from boxing.

Tyson, who turned 31 Monday, bit both of Holyfield's ears during the third round of their World Boxing Association title bout, apparently enraged over a cut he sustained in a head-butting clash in the second round that was ruled unintentional.
"I apologise to the world, to my family and to the Nevada State Athletic Commission that has always treated me fairly," Tyson said in his prepared statement.
Holyfield was taken to the hospital after the fight to have his right ear repaired.
Keach, Tyson's lawyer, said that in his own opinion the disqualification was sufficent punishment for Tyson.
"I've been reading so much in the press that Mike should be banned or whatever," he said, calling for "a fair disposition of the case."
